subject: maths-aa-sl
author: original (NevaIB)
title: Financial applications of geometric sequences

points.text: Compound interest with k compounding periods per year
Annual depreciation as a negative rate; solving for time, rate or value (GDC finance solver allowed)

bigPicture: Compound interest and depreciation are geometric sequences with money. The formula is given; the skill is reading the rate, the number of periods per year and the direction of rounding.

keyIdeas.cue: Compound interest with k compounding periods a year?
keyIdeas.answer: FV = PV(1 + r/(100k))^(kn): r is the annual rate in %, k the periods per year, n the years.

keyIdeas.cue: Depreciation, and how do you find n, r or PV?
keyIdeas.answer: Depreciation is a negative rate: value = PV(1 − r/100)^n. To find an unknown, use the GDC finance (TVM) solver or logs; on the TVM solver money paid out and money received have opposite signs. Round time up when the question asks when a value is first exceeded.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you find the real value of an investment when prices are rising?
keyIdeas.answer: First grow the money at the interest rate to get its future (nominal) value. Then divide by (1 + i/100)^n, where i % is the yearly inflation rate, to express it in today's money. A common shortcut on the TVM solver is to use (interest rate − inflation rate) as the rate; follow the method the question asks for.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you find a depreciation rate from two values?
keyIdeas.answer: value after n years ÷ starting value = (1 − r/100)^n. Take the positive nth root to get the yearly multiplier (between 0 and 1), then r = 100 × (1 − multiplier).

workedExamples.title: Monthly compounding
workedExamples.prompt: 5000 CHF invested at 3% a year, compounded monthly, for 4 years.

misconceptions.right: After 9 years it has not yet passed the target: 10 years.

misconceptions.wrong: Year-end balances of an account paying 6 % a year compounded monthly grow by 1.06 each year.
misconceptions.right: Each year multiplies the balance by (1 + 6/1200)¹² ≈ 1.0617, so the year-end balances are geometric with that ratio.
log 0.9 is negative, so dividing by it flips the sign: n > 6.58, so n = 7.

misconceptions.wrong: Savings plans with regular deposits and loan repayment schedules are AA SL syllabus points.
misconceptions.right: AA SL 1.4 is about compound interest and depreciation (with the GDC finance solver allowed). Regular-payment models belong to the Applications and Interpretation course.

practice.prompt: A machine bought for 8000 CHF loses 25% of its value each year. Write an expression for its value after n years and find its value after 2 years.
commonErrors: Subtracting 25% of the original each year

practice.prompt: 2000 CHF is invested at 4.5% a year compounded quarterly. Find the least number of whole years until it exceeds 3000 CHF.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
